subject: Elmbridge: evidence for delegated log retention and tenant-specific deletion proof
messages:
From: Sophie Carter <sophie.carter@elmbridge.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@elmbridge.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence request: delegated retention and tenant deletion proof

Hi Olga,

We're completing the SIG and CAIQ mapping for Elmbridge and have a few outstanding asks around tenant-scoped log retention and evidence of deletion when customers request data removal. Specifically:

- Can Redwood demonstrate tenant-level TTL enforcement (how it's configured and enforced)?
- We need a small, redacted sample showing a deletion event for tenant "elmbridge-prod" (headers + audit line with timestamp).
- Any attestation you can provide that backups/archival copies are subject to the same deletion policy or the timeline for scrub from backups.
- Mapping to relevant CAIQ/SIG sections would be helpful.

Timing: procurement would like the artifacts by EOD 2027-06-23 to close the security review.

I've attached the SIG questions we filed. If you need scope clarification (system logs vs app logs) let me know; ideally we cover both but we can start with app access logs.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Carter
Head of Procurement, Elmbridge Health
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Carter <sophie.carter@elmbridge.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: delegated retention and tenant deletion proof

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Neha (security engineering) for the technical artifacts and Marcus (account lead) for procurement coordination.

High-level answers up front:
- Redwood supports tenant-scoped TTL and tenant-specific deletion (we store tenant metadata and apply lifecycle rules scoped to tenant prefixes).
- For evidence we can provide: (1) a signed deletion attestation for the requested tenant, (2) a redacted log export that includes the deletion/audit line and surrounding context, and (3) a mapping doc tying those controls to CAIQ/SIG IDs.
- Backups: we run backup lifecycle compaction — cold backups are pruned according to the same tenant TTL policy; complete scrub may take up to 30 days for legacy snapshots depending on snapshot depth. We will include the timeline and runbook references.

Two quick confirmation questions before we assemble artifacts:
1) Do you want the sample to include object names/tenant IDs or should we provide hashed/salted identifiers?
2) When you say "deletion event" — do you require a time-of-deletion hash / signed certificate, or will a deletion-attestation PDF plus the log sample suffice?

If we get those answers today we'll aim to deliver the sample + attestation by EOD 2027-06-23. Marcus, can you pick up the DocuSign/contract variance if Elmbridge needs a formal one-time exception for forensic holds?

— Olga
Olga Petrov
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Sophie Carter <sophie.carter@elmbridge.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: delegated retention and tenant deletion proof

Hi Sophie / Olga — adding the technical details and what we'll attach. Below is the precise deletion flow and the artifacts we'll generate:

Deletion flow (short):
- Customer request hits the control plane; request is recorded in audit log with request_id and tenant_id.
- Policy engine marks tenant prefix objects with a tombstone marker and issues lifecycle rule (S3 lifecycle-style) scoped to tenant prefix.
- Hot storage immediate deletion: objects under the tenant prefix are removed from serving cluster within minutes; a deletion-audit event is emitted with timestamp (ISO8601) and request_id.
- Background compaction/backup scrub: snapshots and cold backups are scanned; objects with tombstone older than retention-window are pruned during nightly compaction. For active snapshots the maximum scrub lag for legacy snapshots is 30 days. Newer incremental snapshot system supports prune-in-7-days for snapshots created after 2026-11.
- KV cache / model artifacts: references are invalidated on deletion; cache entries expire immediately and any long-lived keys are rotated.

Artifacts we'll produce for Elmbridge:
1) redwood_deletion_attestation-elmbridge.pdf — signed by our Compliance lead, includes: request_id, tenant hash (sha256), deletion timestamp, scope (app logs + access logs), and statement on backup scrub timeline.
2) log-retention-sample-elmbridge.csv — small redacted CSV (10 lines) containing: event_time, tenant_hash, request_id, event_type (deletion), object_path (redacted), and deletion_certificate_hash.
3) mapping_doc_caig_sig.txt — mapping of the controls to CAIQ/SIG IDs (we'll include the relevant IDs for data-retention, deletion, and backup handling).

Notes and asks:
- We'll hash tenant IDs using salted SHA256 by default; if Elmbridge needs original tenant IDs for their internal correlation we can provide them under an NDA channel.
- For the time-of-deletion hash you mentioned: we can include a signed hash line in the sample (deletion_certificate_hash) and the attestation PDF will include the signature metadata.
- We'll deliver artifacts via a secure Drive folder; please confirm the email (sophie.carter@elmbridge.ai) is ok for access once Marcus confirms DocuSign coordination.

Attachments referenced: redwood_deletion_attestation-elmbridge.pdf, log-retention-sample-elmbridge.csv, mapping_doc_caig_sig.txt

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sophie Carter <sophie.carter@elmbridge.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, legal@elmbridge.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 14:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: delegated retention and tenant deletion proof

Thanks — this looks good and aligns with our auditors' needs. A few quick clarifications:

- Tenant hashing is fine; please include salted SHA256 and indicate the salt method in the mapping_doc_caig_sig.txt.
- We do require the deletion_certificate_hash line in the sample (that should match the attestation PDF).
- For backups: Elmbridge requires a one-time variance workflow for up to 90-day forensic holds for a small subset of tenants (details in the attached SIG questions). Marcus, can you coordinate a short DocuSign amendment to the renewal that covers this conditional exception?

If you can drop the artifacts into the secure folder by EOD 6/23 that's perfect. We may follow up with a couple of CAIQ question IDs after our security team maps your mapping doc.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Sophie
